To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
public participation is an emerging arena for computer-mediated information and communication activities in disaster response that can be characterized as an expanding set of information pathways.
the public's use of ICTs in crisis situations creates a new information ecology in which public participation becomes a key element of disaster response.

the future of citizen communications in crisis is likely to be one of ICT-supported public interaction, which will be characterized by the emergence of new information pathways that serve different functions and that are not well aligned with the command-and-control models used by formal response organizations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role ICT can play in the future of disaster response.
understanding the emerging role of ICT in disaster response as an enabler of public participation, and with anticipating how this role will develop over the coming decades.
anticipating a future of citizen communications in crisis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the future of citizen communications in crisis is not yet written.
the future of ICT-supported citizen communications in crisis is uncertain, but the need for it is clear.
the role of ICT in crisis response is not yet clear.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the future of ICT-supported disaster response is in a complex mix of public participation, formal response, and informal activities, and that the information science research agenda should include the analysis of public participation in disaster contexts.
ICT-supported public participation will be a key feature of the future of public response in disasters.
ICT-supported citizen communication is a critical, but largely unanticipated, component of the post-impact response landscape.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the public is an important actor in disaster response.
the future of ICT in disaster response will be shaped by the emerging public participation arena.
the emerging information pathways of public participation in response to crisis need more attention from information science researchers.
